summary: This bill requires the President to block any U.S.-supplied weapons or military equipment from being used against Christian churches, religious sites, or civilians in foreign countries.

scores.thoughts: The bill imposes restrictions on how US-provided weapons may be used abroad but contains no provisions that alter federal spending levels, appropriations, or budgets in any way.
No provisions address taxes, tax policy, rates, or revenue collection.
The legislation has no connection to healthcare systems, coverage, or policy.
The bill concerns foreign use of US-supplied weapons and does not address domestic firearm regulations or gun rights.
No provisions relate to immigration, borders, visas, or refugee policy.
The bill does not engage with reproductive rights or abortion policy.
While the bill references weapons and implements of war supplied to foreign countries, it does not change defense spending levels or appropriations; it only adds usage restrictions.
No environmental or climate-related provisions are present.
The legislation has no bearing on welfare programs or social safety net policies.
No connection to education policy, schools, or funding.
The bill does not address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related policies.
No provisions touch on sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
The bill contains nothing related to trade agreements, tariffs, or globalization.
No fiscal provisions affect deficits, debt reduction, or spending priorities.
The legislation does not address LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
The bill conditions the use of US-supplied weapons to foreign countries but does not alter the overall level or amount of foreign or military aid provided.
No provisions relate to voting access, election integrity, or electoral processes.
The bill has no connection to technology regulation or data privacy.
No labor, union, or employment provisions are included.
The bill protects Christian properties and civilians abroad from US weapons but does not engage with the domestic balance between religious exemptions and anti-discrimination laws.
